channel.title: S. Markakis — Blog
channel.description: Cybersecurity research, CTF writeups, and development notes by S. Markakis.

item.title: HTB: Support
item.description: HackTheBox Support — an easy Active Directory box rooted entirely from macOS: a leaked .NET tool on an anonymous SMB share decompiles to a hardcoded, XOR-obfuscated LDAP password; that account's directory read finds another password stashed in the support user's info attribute for a WinRM foothold; and a GenericAll over the DC object drives a Resource-Based Constrained Delegation chain to Domain Admin — done with ilspycmd, ldapsearch and pure-Python impacket, no Windows attack host.

item.title: HTB: Orion
item.description: HackTheBox Orion — Craft CMS 5.6.16 falls to the pre-auth Yii2 PhpManager gadget chain (CVE-2025-32432); when access-log poisoning is blocked by a stale marker from a prior attacker, a session-file poisoning variant gets around it for RCE as www-data. A .env leak hands over DB creds, a cracked bcrypt hash gets SSH as adam, and a loopback-only GNU Inetutils telnetd trusts the client's USER environment variable (CVE-2026-24061) for a passwordless root login.

item.title: HTB: SmartHire
item.description: HackTheBox SmartHire — an MLOps box: a hidden models. subdomain runs MLflow 2.14.1 with default admin:password, CVE-2024-37054 turns a trained model into a cloudpickle deserialization RCE for a shell as svcweb, and a NOPASSWD sudo rule on mlflowctl.py is escalated to root via a group-writable plugins/dev directory where a dropped .pth file executes at interpreter startup.

item.title: HTB: Pirate
item.description: HackTheBox Pirate — a full Active Directory chain driven from macOS: a pre-Windows 2000 machine account still holding its bootstrap password bootstraps Kerberos, a readable gMSA gives WinRM on the DC, an NTLM-relay + PrinterBug coercion plants RBCD on an internal web server to recover a domain user, a ForceChangePassword unlocks a delegation account, and SPN-jacking a constrained-delegation SPN onto the DC yields Domain Admin.

item.title: HTB: Connected
item.description: HackTheBox Connected — a FreePBX 16 two-CVE web RCE (CVE-2025-57819 unauthenticated stacked SQLi into an admin, then CVE-2025-61678 authenticated firmware-upload path traversal to a webshell), then root via the FreePBX sysadmin incron hook, whose signature check trusts an editable module.sig it never GPG-verifies.

item.title: HTB: Enigma
item.description: HackTheBox Enigma — an anonymous NFS export leaks onboarding creds, password reuse into webmail leaks CRM creds, an OpenSTAManager P7M command injection (CVE-2025-69212) lands a webshell, a cracked DB hash gives a user, and a root-run OliveTin automation tool executes attacker-controlled arguments for root.

item.title: HTB: DevHub
item.description: HackTheBox DevHub — unauthenticated RCE in MCPJam Inspector (CVE-2026-23744), a leaked Jupyter token for code execution as analyst, and a hidden root-run MCP tool with a hardcoded API key that dumps root's SSH private key.

item.title: HTB: Checkpoint
item.description: HackTheBox Checkpoint — Active Directory tombstone reanimation, a malicious VS Code .vsix extension for RCE, the Server 2025 BadSuccessor dMSA privilege escalation, and dumping a domain admin hash out of a VMware memory snapshot with volatility3.

item.title: HTB: Reactor
item.description: React Server Components prototype-pollution RCE (CVE-2025-55182) into a Next.js dashboard, an unsalted MD5 cracked to an SSH password, and a root Node.js Inspector bound to loopback driven over the DevTools protocol for root.

item.title: What a Penetration Test Is — and Isn't
item.description: A buyer's guide for business owners: what a real pentest involves, why an automated scan report isn't one, what the deliverables are, and the questions (and red flags) before you pay.

item.title: MikroTik: Centralised Wi-Fi with CAPsMAN
item.description: Manage every access point in a hotel from one place — RouterOS 7 CAPsMAN (WifiWave2): the manager, provisioning CAPs, one config for all radios, VLAN-tagged SSIDs, seamless roaming, and the discovery gotchas.

item.title: Why Guest Wi-Fi Needs Its Own Network
item.description: A plain-language guide for hotel and business owners: what network segmentation is, why a Wi-Fi password protects nothing by itself, and the five things to ask your IT person for — including proof.

item.title: MikroTik: Hotspot & Captive Portal for Hotels
item.description: A guest Wi-Fi login page done right — the hotspot, a branded terms-acceptance login, voucher codes with User Manager, RADIUS, a walled garden, per-guest bandwidth, and the HTTPS-redirect reality every hotel hits.

item.title: MikroTik RouterOS Fundamentals — A 13-Part Series
item.description: A complete, practical RouterOS course in 13 writeups — from terminal habits and backups through VLANs, firewalling, WireGuard, OSPF, and a full hotel-network lab. The MikroTik counterpart to our 27-part Cisco series.

item.title: HTB: FireFlow
item.description: Langflow 1.8.2 unauthenticated RCE, MCP service JWT cryptographic bypass, and a multi-stage Kubernetes escape via kubelet WebSocket exec and privileged container mounts.

item.title: MikroTik Lab: The Hotel Network, Start to Finish
item.description: A complete hotel network on MikroTik — RB5009 gateway, CRS326 core, VLAN-tagged SSIDs, guest isolation firewall, per-VLAN DHCP, and PCQ fairness — built in order, verified, then failure-drilled. Runs on CHR too.

item.title: Cohort — HackTheBox
item.description: Easy machine walkthrough — SSRF filter bypass via alternate IP encoding, pre-auth RCE in Marimo notebook, and a PackageKit TOCTOU race condition for root.

item.title: HTB: Paperwork
item.description: OS command injection in a hand-rolled LPD/RFC 1179 intake service, a decorative path sanitiser in a JetDirect/PJL printer emulator, and a root daemon that leaks an open file descriptor to a root-only credential file over SCM_RIGHTS.

item.title: MikroTik: OSPF on RouterOS 7 — and Talking to Cisco
item.description: OSPF in RouterOS 7's rebuilt routing engine — instance, area, interface-template — on a three-router topology where one router is a Cisco. Mixed-vendor adjacency, costs, default origination, and the ROS6→7 migration traps.

item.title: MikroTik: WireGuard VPN
item.description: WireGuard on RouterOS 7 from zero — road-warrior access for phone and laptop, a site-to-site tunnel between offices, the allowed-address logic everyone gets wrong, and the keepalive trick for peers behind NAT.

item.title: MikroTik: The RouterOS Firewall, Properly
item.description: Connection tracking, a default-deny input chain that can't lock you out, a forward chain with FastTrack that doesn't break QoS, and address-list rate-limiting for brute-force — built from first principles.

item.title: Cisco Lab: The Broken Campus — Eight Faults
item.description: A troubleshooting scenario: the part-24 campus with eight planted faults — wrong VLANs, err-disabled ports, a pruned trunk, split-brain HSRP, a missing DHCP relay, a stale NAT ACL. Diagnose each from the symptom, layer by layer.

item.title: Cisco Lab: HQ + Branches — GRE over IPsec WAN
item.description: A hub-and-spoke WAN you can build in Packet Tracer — an ISP cloud that refuses to route your LANs, GRE tunnels that carry them anyway, OSPF over the tunnels, and IPsec encrypting the lot.

item.title: Cisco Lab: Multi-Area OSPF
item.description: Five routers, three areas — ABRs, the LSA types that matter, stub and totally-stubby areas, default-information originate, and cost tuning with a failure drill. Builds fully in Packet Tracer.

item.title: Cisco Lab: The Collapsed-Core Campus
item.description: A complete Packet Tracer campus build — two access switches, two L3 cores with HSRP and aligned Rapid-PVST roots, an LACP core interlink, and a NAT edge. Full topology, addressing plan, and failure drills.

item.title: Cisco IOS Fundamentals — The Complete 27-Part Series
item.description: A complete, practical Cisco IOS course in 27 writeups — from your first console session to firewalls, redundancy, automation, and four full Packet Tracer lab scenarios. Every post cross-mapped to MikroTik.

item.title: Buying Used Cisco Switches: Smart or Trap?
item.description: A practical guide to buying refurbished Cisco gear for an SMB — whats safe to buy used, spotting counterfeits, the licensing and support catch, EOL/security-patch risk, and a pre-purchase checklist.

item.title: Catalyst vs Meraki for a Small Business — An Honest Take
item.description: Cisco Catalyst (CLI, one-time cost) or Meraki (cloud dashboard, subscription)? An honest, vendor-neutral comparison for SMBs — the licensing trap, when each wins, and what happens if you stop paying.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Managing a Fleet with Ansible
item.description: Config as code for Cisco — Ansible with the cisco.ios collection: inventory, ios_facts, idempotent ios_config, backups, vaulted secrets, and pushing a change to every switch at once, safely with check mode.

item.title: Cisco IOS: IPv6 Fundamentals
item.description: IPv6 on Cisco without the fear — address types, link-local, SLAAC vs DHCPv6, enabling routing, static routes and OSPFv3, NDP instead of ARP, and why theres no NAT.

item.title: Cisco IOS: SPAN & RSPAN Port Mirroring
item.description: Copy traffic to an analyzer without a tap — local SPAN, remote RSPAN across switches, and ERSPAN over IP on Cisco: sources, destinations, the oversubscription gotcha, and IDS/incident-response use.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Management-Plane Hardening
item.description: Audit and lock down any Cisco device in 15 minutes — SSH ciphers, SNMPv3, AAA, VTY access-class, control-plane policing, unused services, and the login-hardening checklist we run on every box.

item.title: Cisco IOS: 802.1X Port Authentication
item.description: Authenticate devices before they get network access — 802.1X with RADIUS on Cisco switches: supplicant/authenticator/server roles, dot1x config, MAB fallback, dynamic VLANs, and open-mode rollout.

item.title: Cisco IOS: EEM On-Box Automation
item.description: Make the router fix itself — Embedded Event Manager applets that react to syslog, timers, and track state: auto-recover err-disabled ports, back up config on change, and alert on events.

item.title: HTB: Nexus
item.description: HackTheBox Nexus machine walkthrough — leaked Gitea commit credentials into an authenticated Krayin CRM file-upload RCE, a leaked .env password reused over SSH, and an automated exploit for a Gitea template-sync path traversal that plants a root SSH key.

item.title: HTB: Abducted
item.description: HackTheBox Abducted machine walkthrough — unauthenticated RCE via a Samba print-spooler %J injection (CVE-2026-4480), credential recovery from an rclone config, SMB symlink key injection, and a systemd drop-in to root.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Upgrading Safely
item.description: Upgrade a Cisco switch or router without bricking it — check space, verify the image hash, set boot variables, and the difference between classic bundle boot and IOS-XE install mode, with a rollback plan.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Observability (NTP, Syslog, SNMP & NetFlow)
item.description: You cant troubleshoot what you didnt record — synchronized time with NTP, centralized logs with syslog, monitoring with SNMPv3, and traffic visibility with Flexible NetFlow on Cisco IOS.

item.title: Detecting Attacks on Cisco Gear
item.description: The blue-team companion to the offensive post — the syslog, NetFlow, and config-change signatures that catch Smart Install/SNMP config theft, DTP/VTP Layer-2 abuse, recon/brute force, and post-compromise changes on Cisco gear.

item.title: Detecting Attacks on MikroTik Gear
item.description: The defender's half of the RouterOS offensive post — off-box detection via the account log topic, Traffic-Flow, and baseline diffing to catch Winbox exploitation, brute force, config exfil/pivoting, and the persistence an attacker leaves behind.

item.title: Network Architecture — Design Guides
item.description: Design-level network architecture — campus topologies, segmentation, WAN and edge, spine-leaf fabrics, perimeter/DMZ, zero trust, out-of-band management, resilience, and SMB reference designs. The why and when above the how.

item.title: Network Architecture: Collapsed-Core vs Three-Tier vs Spine-Leaf
item.description: The campus/DC topology decision — when a collapsed core, a three-tier hierarchy, or a spine-leaf fabric each wins, traded on device count, failure domain, and bandwidth predictability, with a one-table decision guide.

item.title: Network Architecture: Designing Segmentation
item.description: How to design segmentation before you configure it — enumerate trust zones by blast-radius, build a default-deny inter-zone matrix, pick the right enforcement per boundary, and address/name it so the design survives.

item.title: Network Architecture: Hub-Spoke vs Mesh vs SD-WAN
item.description: Choosing the multi-site WAN shape — centralised hub-and-spoke, fast-but-quadratic full mesh, or controller-brokered SD-WAN — and why dynamic-shortcut overlays give much of SD-WAN's benefit without the subscription.

item.title: Network Architecture: The Multihomed Edge
item.description: Designing a resilient internet edge — provider-assigned dual-WAN vs provider-independent BGP, active/backup vs active/active, and where NAT/CGNAT belongs (including the double-NAT and Starlink-CGNAT traps).

item.title: Network Architecture: Spine-Leaf & VXLAN/EVPN
item.description: The modern DC/large-campus fabric demystified — a routed ECMP spine-leaf underlay, a VXLAN overlay floating Layer-2 tenants on Layer-3, and EVPN as the BGP control plane that makes it scale.

item.title: Network Architecture: Perimeter & DMZ Design
item.description: Where internet-facing services should live — three-legged vs screened-subnet firewall placement, the load-bearing DMZ-to-LAN deny rule, east-west discipline inside the DMZ, and safe publishing patterns.

item.title: Network Architecture: Zero-Trust Segmentation
item.description: Zero trust minus the marketing — never trust location, least privilege, assume breach — as identity-driven microsegmentation, and how to capture the 80/20 on Cisco/MikroTik you already own instead of a ZTNA platform.

item.title: Network Architecture: The Out-of-Band Management Network
item.description: Why you can't fix a down network over the down network — designing an isolated management plane, console-server access to a box with no IP, and an independent recovery uplink, for resilience and security.

item.title: Network Architecture: Designing for Failure
item.description: A systematic SPOF audit across power, links, devices, WAN, protocols and services — matching redundancy to the cost of downtime, testing failover by causing failure, and the single points everyone forgets.

item.title: Network Architecture: SMB Reference Designs
item.description: Proven small-business blueprints — the common skeleton (collapsed-core, dual-WAN, six zones) plus the trade-specific twist for a hotel, a clinic, and a professional office, distilled from real builds.

item.title: Cisco Wireless: The Lightweight AP Architecture
item.description: Controller-based Cisco wireless — how a lightweight AP discovers and joins a WLC over CAPWAP (DHCP option 43/DNS/broadcast), the Catalyst 9800 tag model for configuring the whole fleet, FlexConnect for branches, and VLAN-per-SSID.

item.title: MikroTik: Standalone Wi-Fi (wifiwave2)
item.description: A single RouterOS AP done right with the wifiwave2 stack — WPA3 transitional security, multiple SSIDs each tagged to its own VLAN, guest client-isolation, and the standalone-vs-CAPsMAN decision that mirrors Cisco autonomous-vs-lightweight.

item.title: MikroTik Lab: Multi-Area OSPF
item.description: Five RouterOS 7 routers across three areas — ABRs via interface-templates, a stub area, the LSA types that matter proven by inspection, and the every-area-touches-the-backbone and MTU-mismatch traps.

item.title: MikroTik Lab: HQ + Branches — GRE over IPsec WAN
item.description: An encrypted, dynamically-routed branch WAN on RouterOS 7 — GRE tunnels carrying OSPF, IPsec via the GRE ipsec-secret one-liner, the protocol-47/MTU gotchas, and passive-LAN/ptp-tunnel hygiene.

item.title: MikroTik Lab: The Broken Network
item.description: Seven realistic RouterOS faults dressed as support tickets — a missing bridge VLAN member, scoped masquerade, OSPF MTU mismatch, DHCP bound to the wrong interface, FastTrack bypassing a rule, per-packet routing-marks splitting flows, and offload killed by a bridge feature — each with the command that finds it.

item.title: Cisco IOS: DMVPN
item.description: Scale a branch WAN without a full mesh — mGRE + NHRP + IPsec, a hub you configure once, dynamic spoke registration, and Phase-3 direct spoke-to-spoke tunnels, with the NBMA-vs-tunnel and routing gotchas.

item.title: MikroTik: Scaling Site-to-Site (Hub-and-Spoke)
item.description: RouterOS has no DMVPN — build the scalable equivalent with a WireGuard hub-and-spoke: one peer per spoke on the hub, OSPF over the overlay, the allowed-address cryptokey-routing trap, and what you trade versus DMVPN's on-demand spoke-to-spoke.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Remote-Access VPN (IKEv2)
item.description: Road-warrior access on IOS — IKEv2/FlexVPN with an authorization policy pushing the client's address, DNS and split-tunnel routes, a virtual-template per client, the server-certificate trust requirement, and an SSL fallback.

item.title: MikroTik: Remote-Access VPN (IKEv2 & SSTP)
item.description: Get laptops and phones securely back to the office on RouterOS — SSTP over TLS/443 for hostile firewalls, IKEv2 with mode-config for native clients, generate-policy and server-cert gotchas, plus the firewall/NAT rules people forget.

item.title: Cisco IOS: EIGRP
item.description: Cisco's advanced distance-vector protocol — named-mode config, the successor/feasible-successor logic behind sub-second failover, unequal-cost load balancing with variance, summarisation, and why it's effectively Cisco-only.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Route Redistribution & BFD
item.description: Glue OSPF, BGP, EIGRP and static together safely — seed metrics and the subnets/E1-vs-E2 traps, tag-and-deny loop prevention, administrative-distance pitfalls, and BFD for millisecond failure detection.

item.title: MikroTik: Route Redistribution & BFD
item.description: RouterOS 7 redistribution through the filter-chain model — per-protocol toggle plus a mandatory output chain, tag-and-reject loop prevention, administrative distance, and version-dependent BFD for fast, stable failover.

item.title: Cisco IOS: BGP & Dual-ISP Multihoming
item.description: Run a real multihomed BGP edge on Cisco IOS — two eBGP upstreams, outbound path control with local-preference, inbound with AS-path prepend, mandatory anti-transit filtering, and automatic failover.

item.title: MikroTik: BGP & Dual-ISP Multihoming
item.description: RouterOS 7 rewrote BGP — build a dual-ISP edge the v7 way with /routing bgp connection and /routing filter chains: two upstreams, local-preference and prepend path control, anti-transit filters, and automatic failover.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Policy-Based Routing
item.description: Route by who sent the packet, not just where it's going — PBR route-maps that steer a subnet or application out a different next-hop, the set-clause differences, and pairing with IP SLA so a dead path never blackholes.

item.title: MikroTik: Policy Routing with Rules & Mangle
item.description: RouterOS's two policy-routing tools — lightweight routing rules and connection-aware mangle routing-marks — when to use which, the connection-mark-then-routing-mark pattern that keeps a flow pinned to one WAN, and per-WAN NAT.

item.title: Cisco IOS-XE: Model-Driven Config (NETCONF/RESTCONF)
item.description: Talk to modern IOS-XE like an API — YANG-modelled config over NETCONF and RESTCONF, a curl RESTCONF quick-win, transactional NETCONF edits with a candidate datastore via ncclient, and when this beats CLI/Ansible.

item.title: MikroTik: RouterOS 7 Containers
item.description: Run OCI/Docker images on the router itself — the device-mode security gate, veth networking on an isolated bridge, pulling and running a container (Pi-hole), persistence with mounts, and the architecture/storage constraints.

item.title: MikroTik: Metrics with Prometheus & Grafana
item.description: Time-series metrics and dashboards for RouterOS — a read-only API user, the mktxp exporter (optionally in a container on the router), a Prometheus scrape job, and Grafana dashboards with alerts on BGP/WAN/CPU/queues.

item.title: Field Notes: Auditing a Small Hotel Group
item.description: An anonymised security audit across three small family hotels — a flat network with guests on the same wire as the booking PC and cameras, an exposed router management plane, and the guest-to-card-data finding that got remediation approved the same afternoon.

item.title: Cisco ↔ MikroTik: The Translation Guide
item.description: The same network task in Cisco IOS and MikroTik RouterOS side by side, grouped by topic, each row linking the full twin post on both platforms — a jump table for a mixed estate.

item.title: MikroTik: First Contact
item.description: Your first ten minutes with a new RouterOS device — WinBox and MAC-connect, the default configuration and how to read it, identity, users, addressing, and a safe way back if you lock yourself out.

item.title: MikroTik: Securing RouterOS
item.description: Lock down a RouterOS box properly — disable the services you don't use, an input-chain firewall that protects the router itself, real user accounts, SSH strong crypto, neighbour-discovery and MAC-server exposure, and the Winbox port you must never leave on the internet.

item.title: MikroTik: DHCP Server & NAT
item.description: Hand out addresses and share one public IP — an IP pool, a DHCP server with reservations, masquerade vs src-nat, and the connection-tracking model that makes RouterOS NAT behave the way it does.

item.title: MikroTik: Bridge & Switch Port Security
item.description: Stop Layer-2 abuse on RouterOS — bridge port isolation with horizon, DHCP snooping and trusted ports, bridge filtering, MAC limits, and why hardware offload changes which of these actually run on the switch chip.

item.title: MikroTik: STP & Bonding
item.description: Loop prevention and link aggregation on RouterOS — RSTP/MSTP bridge modes, root-bridge and port cost, and 802.3ad LACP bonding to double a link between switches without a loop.

item.title: MikroTik: VRRP First-Hop Redundancy
item.description: Two RouterOS boxes, one virtual gateway — VRRP so the LAN keeps its default gateway when a router dies, with priorities, preemption, and the interface-tracking trick that fails over on a dead WAN, not just a dead router.

item.title: MikroTik: Logging, SNMP & Traffic-Flow
item.description: Make a RouterOS box tell you what it's doing — remote syslog, SNMPv3 monitoring, NTP so timestamps mean something, and Traffic-Flow (NetFlow/IPFIX) export to see what's actually on the wire.

item.title: MikroTik: Upgrading RouterOS Safely
item.description: Update RouterOS without bricking a remote site — release channels, the two-part package-plus-RouterBOARD-firmware upgrade everyone forgets, backups before you touch it, and a clean rollback path.

item.title: MikroTik: 802.1X Port Authentication
item.description: Require identity before a port passes traffic — RouterOS 7 dot1x server against a RADIUS backend, supplicant basics, and the fallback VLAN for devices that can't authenticate.

item.title: MikroTik: Packet Sniffer & Port Mirror
item.description: See the actual packets on RouterOS — the switch-chip port mirror for line-rate SPAN, the built-in /tool sniffer with quick-filters, and streaming capture straight into Wireshark over TZSP.

item.title: MikroTik: IPv6 Fundamentals
item.description: Turn on IPv6 the right way on RouterOS — enabling the package, addressing and SLAAC, DHCPv6-PD to hand your ISP's prefix to the LAN, router advertisements, and an IPv6 firewall so you don't accidentally expose everything.

item.title: MikroTik: Managing a Fleet
item.description: Configure many RouterOS boxes without logging into each one — the RouterOS 7 REST API, the Ansible community.routeros collection, and a scripted config-push pattern that stays idempotent.

item.title: Attacking MikroTik Gear — A Pentester's Field Guide
item.description: The offensive companion to the RouterOS series: what an attacker actually does to a MikroTik — Winbox discovery and the CVE-2018-14847 credential leak, default-account and API exposure, bandwidth-test abuse, post-exploitation, and the one-line fix for each.

item.title: Field Notes: A Cisco Campus for a Cretan Hotel
item.description: An anonymised field write-up of a real collapsed-core Cisco build for a seaside hotel in Crete: VLAN segmentation for guests / PMS / CCTV / VoIP, dual-WAN failover with fibre primary and Starlink backup, guest isolation, and the three things that actually broke.

item.title: MikroTik ↔ Cisco — One IPsec Tunnel, Two Vendors
item.description: Build a working site-to-site IKEv2 IPsec tunnel between a Cisco IOS router and a MikroTik RouterOS box — the exact proposal matching, the route-based-vs-policy-based mismatch that breaks it, and NAT exemption on both ends.

item.title: Attacking Cisco Gear — A Pentester's Field Guide
item.description: The offensive companion to the IOS series: what an attacker actually does to a Cisco switch or router — CDP/SNMP recon, Smart Install config theft, SNMP-RW config exfil, type-7/5/8/9 password cracking, and DTP/VTP Layer-2 abuse — with the one-line fix for each.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Site-to-Site IPsec VPN
item.description: Connect two offices over the internet securely — an IKEv2 route-based (VTI) IPsec tunnel on Cisco IOS: proposals, keyring, profile, tunnel interface, routing, and the NAT-exemption gotcha.

item.title: Cisco IOS: QoS for VoIP
item.description: Make voice calls survive a busy link — DSCP marking, trust boundaries, LLQ priority queuing for RTP, and the class-based policy that keeps phones clear when the WAN is saturated.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Zone-Based Firewall
item.description: A real stateful firewall on an IOS router — zones, class-maps, policy-maps, zone-pairs, and stateful inspection. The stateful upgrade from stateless ACLs, built step by step.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Dual-WAN Failover with IP SLA
item.description: Failover that detects a dead ISP even when the link stays up — IP SLA probes, track objects, tracked static routes, and NAT that follows the active WAN.

item.title: Cisco IOS: First-Hop Redundancy (HSRP & VRRP)
item.description: A redundant gateway that survives a dead router — HSRP and VRRP explained: virtual IP, active/standby election, interface tracking, load sharing, and the preempt gotcha.

item.title: Cisco IOS: STP & EtherChannel
item.description: Why one port is always blocking — spanning tree explained: root bridge election, Rapid PVST+, PortFast, and bundling redundant links into an LACP EtherChannel that uses them all.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Static Routing & OSPF
item.description: How a Cisco router chooses paths — reading the routing table, static and default routes, floating statics for failover, and single-area OSPF that maintains itself.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Switch Security
item.description: Hardening Cisco access switches — port security and sticky MACs, err-disabled recovery, DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection, BPDU guard, and unused-port hygiene.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Access Control Lists
item.description: Filtering traffic on a Cisco router — standard vs extended ACLs, wildcard masks, named ACLs with sequence numbers, where to apply them, and protecting the VTY lines.

item.title: Cisco IOS: DHCP & NAT/PAT
item.description: Hand out addresses and share one public IP on a Cisco router — DHCP pools and exclusions, DHCP relay, NAT concepts, PAT (overload) for the whole LAN, and static NAT for port forwarding.

item.title: Cisco IOS: Backup & Restore
item.description: Protect a Cisco config — save to startup, export to TFTP/SCP, automate with the archive feature and kron, roll back with configure replace, and recover a locked device.

item.title: Cisco IOS: VLANs & Trunking
item.description: Segmenting a Cisco switch network — access ports, 802.1Q trunks, the native VLAN, and inter-VLAN routing with router-on-a-stick and an L3 switch (SVI).

item.title: Cisco IOS: First Contact
item.description: Your first hour on a Cisco switch or router — the IOS CLI from scratch: console access, the three command modes, safe show commands, basic setup, and enabling SSH.

item.title: Starlink + MikroTik Failover
item.description: Multi-WAN failover on RouterOS v7 — keep a remote Starlink site online with recursive routing, connection marking, NAT, and netwatch health checks.

item.title: MikroTik: Backup and Recovery
item.description: Export vs binary backup on MikroTik RouterOS — when to use which, how to automate both, and the full Netinstall recovery procedure.

item.title: MikroTik: RouterOS Scripting
item.description: RouterOS scripting basics — variables, conditionals, loops, functions, and the scheduler, with WoL, Telegram alerts, and auto-backup examples.

item.title: MikroTik: VLANs
item.description: Configuring VLANs on MikroTik RouterOS — bridge VLAN filtering, tagging, and inter-VLAN routing.

item.title: MikroTik: QoS
item.description: Quality of Service on MikroTik — queue trees, simple queues, and traffic prioritization.

item.title: MikroTik: Port Forwarding
item.description: Setting up dst-nat port forwarding rules on MikroTik RouterOS for inbound services.

item.title: MikroTik: Wake-on-LAN
